alignments.note: The repetition verb is rendered adverbially as again.
The optative idiom supplies Oh that ... were; its object suffix separately realizes I. Neither who nor give has an independent English rendering.
As in renders the comparative relation to a temporal setting.
When expresses the temporal construct relation between days and its dependent clause, rather than an independently supplied subordinator.
The infinitive's subject suffix is unexpressed in the recasting with lamp as subject.
The printed upon governs; the alternative above is not aligned.
No conjunction stands before the second colon.
Through expresses the bare noun's adverbial path function under rule 33.
The comparative-relative compound has one rendering, As; its governing preposition heads.
The ASV reverses the nominal relation: days becomes the English dependent, carrying of.
Ripeness renders autumn figuratively. The margin's literal order does not override the printed recasting.
The printed friendship, rather than the marginal counsel, is aligned.
The copula belongs to the prepositional predicate.
The relational predicate carries the construction-supplied copula.
The Hebrew juxtaposes the second clause without a conjunction.
The prepositional object becomes a bare indirect object.
To expresses the bare destination noun's case-function.
The printed street is aligned, not the marginal broad place.
The second finite clause has no temporal subordinator. Repeating the opening temporal preposition's rendering is an alternative; the asyndetic independent finite clause favors a supplied when.
Young carries the youth lexeme; men supplies the generic human class.
The reflexive realizes the verb's voice.
No conjunction joins the two Hebrew verbs.
The noun words is recast as talking.
Hand has no possessive suffix; the written suffix supplies their mouth, not an additional possessive on hand.
The figurative hushed is aligned rather than the margin's literal hid.
Roof specifies the palate; mouth alone loses that specificity, so roof heads the expanded nominal.
For when renders the subordinating כי; when is repeated over the coordinated eye clause. For is an alternative head, but when carries the clause's temporal subordination.
No object morpheme accompanies heard.
No object morpheme accompanies saw.
The second apodosis has no written English connective.
Witness carries the verb's lexeme; unto connects its object suffix under rule 44.
The articleless participle follows and modifies poor; its attributive relative stays with it.
The printed text subordinates this clause without a separate coordinator; the margin's and him is not the target.
The helper participle is recast as to help.
The possessive preposition carries had.
The suffix is realized as the relative subject that and the direct pronoun him. The direct pronoun heads, rather than the relative recasting.
The substantival participle takes its supplied antecedent and relative; of expresses its construct dependence.
The supplied determiner belongs to the English possessor.
Sing is the lexical predicate in the causative rendering; for joy completes its joyful-singing sense.
The printed active rendering governs rather than the marginal reflexive alternative.
The comparative prepositional predicate carries was.
The written copular verb is realized again as was in the coordinated second clause under rule 34; its explicit second subject is separate.

The printed text construes this as a headless relative denoting the person whose cause was investigated, taking of him that with I knew. The margin instead makes cause the antecedent; that alternative is set aside.
The object suffix resumes the fronted cause, which English expresses only once.
Cohortative ending.
The printed jaws is aligned, not the literal marginal great teeth.
The printed in governs rather than the margin's beside or literal with.
Days has no possessive morpheme.
Spread out renders the participial predicate, with its construction-supplied copula; the margin's opened is not the target.
The printed to is retained rather than the marginal by.
Night carries the verb's overnight-staying sense; lieth alone loses it. Lieth is the alternative syntactic head, but rule 44 favors the lexical complement.
Ear carries the hearing lexeme in the light-verb rendering.
Men is a supplied lexical subject, not a pronoun realizing verbal inflection.
Silence carries the verb's lexeme.
Again carries the repeating lexeme; spake supplies the contextual action. Spake is an alternative syntactic head, but losing again loses what שנה specifically contributes.
As for expresses the comparison to the object of waiting; for is an English helper within this comparative rendering.
Rain names the lexical precipitation class, while latter specifies its season; latter is the alternative specificity-based head.
The second colon supplies a comparison where Hebrew writes only the purpose preposition for; its as is not governed by the first colon's local comparative phrase.
Had confidence is the verb's own believing/trusting rendering; confidence carries its lexeme.
The Hebrew finite clause has no temporal subordinator.
Paragogic nun.
Chose out renders the selecting verb as a phrasal expression.
As expresses the bare nominal's role under rule 33, despite addition markup.
The printed headless relative supplies one that to the written relative; As separately realizes the comparative preposition, so fusion is unnecessary.
